item.title: What we learned from the Jets' loss to the Bills in Week 10
item.description: The New York Jets were once again embarrassed on Sunday . They were blown out 31-12 by their AFC East rival Buffalo Bills in Week 10 . Head coach Aaron Glenn is now 0-9 all-time in divisional contests. It marked the Jets' fifth-consecutive defeat, and third straight where they've allowed the opposing offense to score 30+ points. Glenn's defense isn't meeting expectations. The hapless Jets are 2-8. With that, Jets Wire has identified three notable happenings from Sunday's latest setback. Braelon Allen should see more carries The workload between Breece Hall and Braelon Allen was more even at running back this week . Hall rushed for a team-high 41 yards, but only averaged 3.7 yards per attempt on 11 carries. Meanwhile, Allen rushed for 5.0 YPC, gaining 40 yards on eight carries. With Hall still coming back from injury, the workload should be an even split. Why can't Omar Cooper Jr. and Kenyon Sadiq be productive? Jets rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. exited Sunday's defeat with an ankle injury . It occcurred on the first offensive series of the game. It was another example of the Jets' struggles to get Cooper and Kenyon Sadiq productive in the same game. Sadiq had three receiving yards after having 49 last weekend. Rookie QB Cade Klubnik isn't ready Jets starting QB Geno Smith also exited with an injury . Rookie quarterback Cade Klubnik replaced him. Klubnik completed 11-of-20 passing attempts for 137 yards, zero touchdowns, and an interception. He won't prevent the Jets from drafting a QB in April. This article originally appeared on Jets Wire: What we learned from the Jets' loss to the Bills in Week 10

item.title: Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph expected to return against Buccaneers
item.description: Kerby Joseph is closing in on playing his first game in more than 13 months. Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell said in his weekly interview Tuesday, Nov. 17, on 97.1 The Ticket (WXYT-FM) that, barring any setbacks, the Lions will activate Joseph this week off the physically unable to perform list with an eye on having him make his season debut Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Joseph has not played since last Oct. 12 because of a cartilage condition in his knee. "I mean, barring anything else here negatively, which there hasn’t been any, he’s progressed nicely here," Campbell said. "The plan would be to get him going this week. Get him going and get him into Tampa Bay and let him play." Campbell did specify how the Lions plan to manage Joseph's snaps against the Bucs and with a quick turnaround to next week's Thanksgiving game against the Chicago Bears . Joseph returned to practice Oct. 26 and took part in position drills for a week before graduating to scout-team duties and team drills last week. INSIDE THE LIONS: Where do Lions turn without Aidan Hutchinson? This time, they're ready His return comes at a time when the Lions are getting good play from their secondary and have depth at safety after the return of Brian Branch and the addition of Andre Cisco , but lost top pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson to a season-ending knee injury. Chuck Clark has started every game at safety, and Branch has joined him in the lineup since he came back from the torn Achilles tendon he suffered last year. Campbell said the Lions likely will be without starting center Cade Mays for another week because of a sprained ankle. Juice Scruggs has played well while starting seven games at center this season. "I don’t see Cade being ready this week," Campbell said. "There’s a chance, but I don’t – I’m not putting all my eggs in that basket. And Juice has been doing a nice job for us. He’s playing really good football. That whole O-line played dang good football the other day." Dave Birkett covers the Lions for the Detroit Free Press. Contact him at dbirkett@freepress.com . item.title: Arch Manning Commits To Senior Day As NFL Draft Clock Ticks
item.description: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images Arch Manning is not hiding from the moment. The Texas quarterback announced Monday that he will participate in the Senior Day ceremonies before the Longhorns face Arkansas on Saturday. The decision secures his place in the pregame tradition, even if he chooses to return to Austin for another season. It does not, however, answer the biggest question surrounding his future: Is this his final college season, or will he put off the NFL Draft for another year? Manning’s stance is clear, even if his future remains a mystery. He told reporters, “I’m a senior, so I’m doing it,” regarding the specific Senior Day events, per reports. The 20-year-old has one season of eligibility left after this year, meaning he could return to Texas in 2027 if he skips the draft. Texas is 8-2 and was ranked No. 6 in the College Football Playoff committee’s most recent rankings, released November 10. The Longhorns have since added a dramatic victory over LSU and remain in contention for a playoff berth. The Quarterback’s Growing Pains A roller-coaster season defined Manning’s time so far. After a thrilling 24-23 September win against Ohio State that earned Texas the No. 1 ranking, the team subsequently dropped two of their following four contests to Florida and Oklahoma. Those losses sparked questions about whether he needed another year to develop his skills. The Longhorns have since won four straight games, including three against ranked opponents like Ole Miss, Missouri, and LSU. This run has restored the buzz around the program and put Manning back in the spotlight. His statistics show a season of considerable progress, but also some costly mistakes. Manning has completed 64.7 percent of his passes for 2,198 yards, 19 touchdowns and 10 interceptions. His three-interception performance against LSU nearly cost Texas the game, but he delivered when it mattered most, throwing the winning touchdown with three seconds remaining. Despite the ups and downs, he insists his college career has “been great.” He told reporters, “I feel like I’ve grown a lot as a person and a player,” according to the New York Post . The pressure to perform is high, but he seems ready to handle it. One Week At A Time The draft question looms large, but Manning refuses to let it distract him. He is focused entirely on the upcoming game against Arkansas rather than what happens after the season ends. “I’ve enjoyed my time, but I’m just focused on this week, winning this week. I’m not really thinking about the future right now,” Manning said, per the New York Post . This mindset keeps the team united and avoids the drama that often plagues senior quarterbacks. The Longhorns still have a shot to host a College Football Playoff game, which would be the perfect stage for a potential final college performance. Whether he leaves for the NFL or stays for another year, the path is set for a big finish.

item.title: AEW’s Adam Copeland reportedly fought a bear, and won
item.description: AEW’s Adam Copeland reportedly fought a bear, and won appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . From acting to pro-wrestling and now even fighting bears, is there anything AEW’s Adam Copeland can’t do? Apparently not. Just a few hours after wrestling at AEW Full Gear against Kazuchika Okada, news came out that Copeland was in a real-life fight with a bear. While Copeland failed to defeat Okada for the AEW International title, the reason for it now might be clear. Bear fights do take a toll, and that was evident after Copeland allegedly defeated one. The Wrestling Observer recently reported that Copeland was in a fight with a bear and apparently, he won, too. As per the report, Copeland was walking with his dogs when he saw a mother bear and her cubs walking toward him. Copeland knew that he had to make himself look bigger to scare the bear, but he was unable to do so because of the dog’s leash in his hands. Instead, without much time to react, Copeland decided to hit the bear under its chin with his shin. The bear was stunned and immediately left the scene. However, following his match at AEW All Out 2026, Copeland announced his decision to retire in 2027. Following his loss to Okada, Copeland was interviewed by Mick Foley. Copeland claimed that he needed to get a few answers and now believes he received them after his Full Gear match. However, the WWE Hall of Famer did not elaborate on what he meant. item.title: Detroit Lions won't ban celebrations after Aidan Hutchinson injury
item.description: Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell said he won’t have a longer discussion with players about what celebrations they should and shouldn’t do after Aidan Hutchinson suffered a season-ending torn ACL while jumping to celebrate a sack in last week’s win over the New England Patriots in Germany. “No. I don’t believe that,” Campbell said Tuesday, Nov. 17, in his weekly interview Tuesday, Nov. 17, on 97.1 The Ticket (WXYT-FM) . “I think what happened speaks for itself and we’re not talking to 8-year-olds here.” Campbell said he believes he tore his bicep one time as a player when he pumped his fist to celebrate a big play he made in a game. Campbell did not specify the game, but in his first season as a Lions tight end in 2006, he tore his triceps and played through the injury while wearing a brace on his arm. “I didn’t tell anybody,” Campbell said. “And I was just excited. I just pumped my arm. And so if you say, ‘Hey, don’t pump your arm next time, make sure you stay stoic.’ Man, this game is built off of emotion and if you have to contain yourself after a play is made – I’m not talking about in the moment, in the game, because you got to keep your head – then you’re really becoming something you’re not.” RELATED: Lions' concern high after Aidan Hutchinson injury: 'He's the heart and soul' Hutchinson hurt his right knee on the final offensive play of the opening series against the Patriots, when he dropped Maye for a 2-yard loss on third-and-13 that forced a field goal. item.title: All About the 2026 F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix, From Top Drivers to Star-Studded Parties
item.description: Las Vegas Grand Prix 2025. The 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix is just around the corner, and there’s plenty of high-octane thrills happening off the grid. Between star-studded parties and events, Sin City has much to offer in the lead-up to the big Formula 1 race on Saturday night, Nov. 21. Now entering its fourth year, F1’s modern street race will take place on a 3.8-mile (6.2 km) temporary street circuit known as the Las Vegas Strip Circuit, lit up by the city’s most iconic landmarks. Drivers competing will pass casinos and attractions such as the Sphere, the Bellagio and more. The Las Vegas Grand Prix is unique because of a stacked on-track schedule, not to mention the support series, like the F1 Academy finale. The paddock is also a who’s who during race weekend, with Formula 1 drivers and the A-List celebrities swarming the scene. item.title: WWE 'Raw': LA Knight joins Cody Rhodes and CM Punk for 'Survivor Series'
item.description: Cody Rhodes arrives on the red carpet at the 2026 ESPY Awards in New York City on July 15, 2026. Rhodes asked LA Knight to join his team for "Survivor Series: WarGames." Photo by John Angelillo/UPI Nov. 17 (UPI) -- LA Knight joined Cody Rhodes and CM Punk's Survivor Series team on WWE Raw . Rhodes and Punk are co-captains for Team USA heading into the Survivor Series: WarGames event where they will be taking on Rey Mysterio's Team Mexico. Team Mexico also already gathered brothers Penta and Rey Fenix for the match, along with Dragon Lee. Team USA also has newcomer Je'Von Evans as a member. Team Mexico and Team USA will battle it out in a traditional five vs. five Survivor Series match. Rhodes and Punk were confronted by The Miz on Monday who demanded to have a spot on Team USA. The Miz mentioned all of his career accolades and how he came up in WWE the same time as Rhodes and Punk did. Knight then arrived onto the scene and joined Team USA, much to The Miz's dismay. Knight then challenged The Miz to a match , with the winner able to compete for Team USA. Knight won the match after nailing The Miz with his Blunt Force Trauma maneuver. Afterwards, The Miz's protege Kit Wilson got involved, leading to Punk taking him out with a GTS followed by a Cross Rhodes by Rhodes. Both Team USA and Team Mexico have one more member that will be announced at a later date. Survivor Series: WarGames takes place in Houston on Nov. 28.

item.title: Infantino challenger Diallo: Football needs a more 'respectful voice'
item.description: FILE PHOTO - FIFA president Gianni Infantino is silhouetted as he walks past the World Cup trophy after addressing the 76th FIFA Congress in Vancouver. (is associated with: «Infantino challenger Diallo: Football needs a more 'respectful voice'») Darryl Dyck/Canadian Press via ZUMA Press/dpa FIFA presidential candidate Philippe Diallo says football's values have been "trampled underfoot" by incumbent Gianni Infantino as he set out his stall ahead of March's election. European governing body UEFA announced on Monday that French Football Federation (FFF) chief Diallo would be its candidate to try to stop Infantino winning a fourth term at the top of the global game. The FFF executive committee unanimously backed Diallo's bid on Tuesday. "I believe I have the experience, the convictions, the values," the 63-year-old told reporters, according to broadcaster RMC. "I want to win, because what is happening has shocked people and does not match the future of football." Infantino is being challenged after a series of controversies, including an aborted attempt to sell off part of the World Cup to an investment group linked to the family of US President Donald Trump. His closeness to Trump, and US forward Folarin Balogun's suspension being lifted at this year's World Cup, angered European football despite Infantino being Swiss and a former UEFA official. "In a democratic process, it is time for someone else to bring a more respectful voice to football," Diallo added. He said he had initially not seen himself as a candidate, but relented after his European colleagues insisted. "The values of our sport have been trampled underfoot. The trust placed in our organization and its president has been broken," Diallo said. "To remain true to my convictions, I could not avoid (the challenge)." There has also been contact with Japanese candidate Kozo Tashima. It is unclear if he will drop out. "If we want to succeed, we must pool our strength and ensure that everyone who shares this vision unites to win," Diallo remarked. UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin decided not to stand but is close to Diallo, who emerged as a candidate after former Arsenal coach and current FIFA functionary Arsène Wenger opted against running. Diallo continued: "There can no longer be a solitary form of leadership in which the major issues of football are decided without any transparency." Infantino took over FIFA in 2016 after an array of scandals beset football's governing body.

item.title: Linda Cohn dismantles ESPN president Burke Magnus over Troy Aikman contract debacle
item.description: Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images ESPN have been battling against the frosty on-screen relationship between Troy Aikman and Joe Buck amid the ongoing contract saga. Monday Night Football rolled through Baltimore this week, and it was clear to see that the ESPN duo’s relationship had not noticeably improved. Aikman’s future remains uncertain with the network as talks over a potential new deal have hit an impasse. Meanwhile, Buck is sitting up in the booth alongside his colleague of many years with a brand new six-year extension worth $108 million. Linda Cohn knows exactly what it is like to work for ESPN having ended her 34-year run with the network earlier this year, and she is disgusted with the manner in which Aikman has been treated. Linda Cohn tears apart ESPN over their handling of Troy Aikman ESPN are considering replacements for Aikman , with the likes of Drew Brees, Greg Olsen and even Peyton Manning being suggested. The former Dallas Cowboys QB has received a lot of praise from Cohn for remaining as professional as he has been amid ESPN’s handling of the situation. “ESPN just butchered this. Burke Magnus, he is in this role, and why did he think that you do one contract and leave the other one hanging in the breeze?” Cohn told Yahoo Sports. “I don’t really put this on Joe Buck. I put it all, and I said this on The Linda Cohn Show, I put it all on ESPN and how they bungled it. You brought it up, Jason: you just don’t do business this way. I don’t care if it’s Troy Aikman or the production assistant that works on First Take, you don’t treat people like this. You really don’t, yet they did, and they did this to Troy Aikman.” Cohn is a legend of ESPN having worked with the network for over three decades. Having departed the company earlier this year, she is now able to speak freely about her thoughts on Burke Magnus and how he is handling the situation surrounding Aikman. “He [Aikman] is such a professional. I don’t know how he is dealing with all this. Let’s think about that for a second: he has to look Joe Buck in the face. I don’t know how the relationship is now; it looks cold as ice right now, of course, over the last month,” she added. “To be able to stand there, be professional, and analyse a football game, and not only do the game for three and a half hours, but do everything that comes with that game (travel, meetings with coaches and players), it is just absolutely absurd.” Read more: Aqib Talib praises ‘exceptional’ QB who’s part of NFL team with a ‘Tom Brady-style offence’ ‘That’s huge’ – Rob Gronkowski so impressed by what he noticed Fernando Mendoza doing on debut Skip Bayless stunned by what Josh Allen has admitted to doing for the Bills

item.title: Yankees Reportedly Made Competitive Offer To Pitcher Who Left Bronx In 2025
item.description: Free agent pitcher Jonathan Loáisiga The New York Yankees have already re-signed Tim Hill and extended a qualifying offer to David Bednar. However, Brian Cashman is focused on adding more relievers. Jonathan Loáisiga has reportedly drawn interest from many teams this offseason, but according to NJ.com's Randy Miller , the Yankees have already made him an offer. "The Yankees have offered a contract to Loáisiga, a source close to the Nicaraguan right-hander told NJ.com," wrote Miller. "The Yankees’ offer is believed to be a one-year deal worth more than Loáisiga’s only other offer, one year for $5 million from the (Arizona) Diamondbacks." According to Miller, Loáisiga is looking for a three-year deal in the $18 million to $20 million range. Loáisiga had a great year for the Diamondbacks, posting a 2.42 ERA in 67 games. He spent eight seasons pitching for the Yankees before last season. The Yankees declined his option last offseason, and he signed a minor league deal with the Diamondbacks. He had a bounce-back year, and now it makes a ton of sense for the Yankees to bring him back. Bringing back Bednar should be one of the Yankees' top priorities, but adding an arm like Loáisiga is also important. The team needs arms that can work in high-leverage situations. Loáisiga reportedly also has interest from the Los Angeles Dodgers, New York Mets and Philadelphia Phillies. There is no guarantee that Loáisiga accepts the Yankees' offer. However, the familiarity in the Bronx could give the Yankees an edge. They have reportedly already surpassed his only other offer to this point. item.title: Giants Legend Headlines 2027 Hall Of Fame Ballot
item.description: San Francisco Giants president of baseball operations Buster Posey The BBWAA unveiled its 2027 Hall of Fame ballot on Monday. The ballot has 27 players, including 14 first-time candidates. Voting concludes Dec. 31 and results will be announced on Jan. 19. The newcomers are led by San Francisco Giants legend Buster Posey and former ace Jon Lester, both of whom won three World Series rings. A seven-time All-Star in his 12 MLB seasons, Posey spent his entire career with the Giants, leading them to a trio of championships in five years from 2010 to 2014. One of the best and most decorated catchers in baseball history, he won an NL Rookie of the Year award, an NL MVP award, a Gold Glove award and five Silver Slugger awards. Now San Francisco's president of baseball operations, Posey is the strongest first-time candidate on the ballot. Time will tell if he gets in right away as his contemporary, Joe Mauer, did in 2024. item.title: Chris Long says it’s so stupid what people are now saying about Mike Vrabel with the Patriots
item.description: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images Chris Long was not a fan of people calling out Mike Vrabel for drinking beer before the New England Patriots’ game against the Detroit Lions on Sunday. A video of Vrabel drinking from a frosted stein at a Munich beer hall made the rounds on the internet. He visited Augustiner Stammhaus, which is a designated Patriots fan pub, to interact with the fans. The video was shared on the Patriots’ official X account and instantly drew reactions from fans. “Listen, I knew we had fans in Germany, I didn’t know we had this many fans. Thank you for your support, go Pats, let’s raise a glass to everybody,” said Vrabel. The criticism continued to follow as the Patriots suffered a 35-10 defeat at the hands of the Lions on Sunday. Chris Long defends Mike Vrabel from beer drinking criticism Long played one season for the Patriots, but does not have much of an affiliation with Vrabel, who took over as head coach almost 8 years after Long left the team. However, he knew how things worked in the NFL, and spoke about how the decision to be at the event was not completely on the head coach. “The beer thing, I hate the look, okay? Like, make no mistake about it. When I saw it, I was like, ‘This is the dumbest s*** in the world. But it reeks of the NFL sending him to this thing on a Saturday, on the way to the hotel, and him coming in for 15 minutes, toasting with fans and drinking half a beer,” said Long on Green Light with Chris Long. “I saw this thing, and my problem is, if I see a bunch of people who don’t understand the context of something but are trying to make a big deal out of it, it drives me f****** nuts. It’s Germany; this is beer culture.” The Patriots’ defeat on Sunday could be more due to the injury to star quarterback Drake Maye, as opposed to Vrabel meeting the fans and having a little beer with them. However, with the Patriots currently holding a 5-5 record, all eyes will be on Vrabel, as he has already had a long offseason of controversy. And with this beer keg incident, it is clear that it is not going to be a great end to the season if the Patriots don’t win games. item.title: Statue planned for Johnny and Matthew Gaudreau at hometown rink
item.description: Johnny Gaudreau and his younger brother, Matthew , will have a statue outside their childhood ice rink in Sewell, New Jersey to honor their lives and hockey careers . item.title: Yankees make offer to coveted free agent reliever
item.description: The Yankees want free agent reliever Jonathan Loaisiga back for their bullpen rebuild after his first injury-free season in 2026 with the Diamondbacks. With lefty Tim Hill re-signed and a qualifying offer extended to closer David Bednar, the Yankees have offered a contract to Loaisiga, a source close to the Nicaraguan right-hander told NJ.com. The source requested anonymity to speak publicly about the situation. The Yankees’ offer is believed to be a one-year deal worth more than Loaisiga’s only other offer, a one-year, $5 million offer from the Diamondbacks. Loaisiga is seeking a three-year deal in the $18 million to $20 million range. The Dodgers, Mets and Phillies also have shown interest. The Yankees went into the offseason with six free-agent relievers and only one of their high-leverage arms under contract for next season: left-hander Brent Headrick. Bednar has until 4 p.m. ET Tuesday to accept a $23.15 million qualifying offer or hit the free agent market. If he passes on the qualifying offer, which is likely, the Yankees are expected to aggressively pursue a three-year deal at a lower annual pay day. Coming off another injury-plagued season in 2025, Loaisiga settled for a minor-league deal with the D’backs last January that included a $1.5 million salary in the majors. He proved to be a bargain, going 7-3 with a 2.42 ERA over a career-high 67 appearances. In addition to reducing homers allowed, Loaisiga averaged 97.9 mph on his sinker, while allowing 1.9 walks per nine innings and a barrel rate of 3.5%. Loaisiga, 32, started his major-league career pitching with the Yankees from 2018-25. He had a breakout season in 2021 when he was 9-4 with a 2.17 ERA in 57 outings, but he was on the injured list 10 times as a Yankee. Loaisiga wants to sign with someone before a probable work stoppage begins Dec. 1 at 11:59 p.m. “I know they want him to sign before the lockout,” the source said. “The Diamondbacks’ offer was weak and they were very clear telling him, ‘We want to lower our payroll.’” Loaisiga picked Arizona because he thought his career would benefit from pitching a full season in a warm-weather city and in the NL West, which is loaded with pitcher-friendly ballparks. “The Dodgers are an option that he likes because of the Los Angeles weather,” the source said. “They are interested, but have not made an offer. Same thing with the Phillies and Mets. No offer.” Loaisiga wants at least a two-year deal so he can get to 10 years’ service and qualify for a full pension. He’s currently at eight years and 22 days. “Two years is important to him because he wants to secure the 10 years,” the source said. As of 2026, a player with 10 years of service time qualifies for a full pension that pays $290,000 annually if the start date is at age 62. Retired players can get a reduced rate starting at age 45. item.title: Steve Kerr explains why Stephen Curry’s longevity is more impressive than that of Steve Nash, John Stockton
item.description: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Steve Kerr explains why Stephen Curry’s longevity is more impressive than that of Steve Nash, John Stockton appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry is out for at least two weeks due to an oblique injury he suffered against the Houston Rockets on November 12. It is the latest ailment for Curry, who has struggled to stay on the court in recent years. He was having a strong campaign before getting sidelined, leading the Warriors to an eight-game winning streak before losing to the Rockets. He was averaging 27.8 points, good for fifth-best in the league, 3.7 rebounds, and 3.9 assists. The Warriors are on a three-game skid, including the defeat to the Rockets, underscoring Curry’s value. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In a report from ESPN’s Anthony Slater, Warriors coach Steve Kerr said they have been extra cautious with the 38-year-old guard’s wear and tear . “The league has never been faster, more athletic, players sprinting around, the ground covered,” said Kerr. “Compared to Steve Nash or John Stockton , other guards of his ilk who were still playing at 38, 39, 40, the game’s a lot harder now.” While it was a sobering truth, Kerr also indirectly conveyed how impressive Curry’s longevity is. For comparison, at 38, Nash averaged 12.7 points, 2.8 rebounds, and 6.7 assists, while Stockton tallied 10.8 points, 2.5 rebounds, and 7.7 assists. They both retired at 41. Kerr is quite familiar with Nash and Stockton. He handled Nash when he was the general manager of the Phoenix Suns. They also reunited on the Warriors, with Nash serving as Kerr’s deputy. The four-time champion coach, meanwhile, had regular battles with Stockton when they were still playing. The Warriors want to have Curry on the floor , but they also need to ensure his long-term health. Handling the “dichotomy,” as Slater put it, of the 12-time All-Star is not easy. “Away from the fireworks show, Curry is in a constant race against time, obsessively evolving his body-maintenance plan in an effort to be available as often as possible—until the clock runs out,” wrote Slater. The clock is perpetually ticking, but Curry is not ready to walk away just yet. item.title: College football AP Top 25 schedule for Week 12 is worst in nearly 20 years
item.description: We have been spoiled with some great college football games each and every week. And with just two regular season weeks left, games should mean more and more. But that might not be the case in Week 12. Of course, the games matter, especially for those teams that are on the bubble of making the College Football Playoff , but in terms of ranked games? There won’t be any. According to On3’s Brett McMurphy , it’s the first time since 2009 that there won’t be any AP Top 25 -ranked matchups in the month of November. Just this past week, we saw five ranked-on-ranked games throughout Saturday. In Week 10, there were even more, with seven games that featured ranked-on-ranked matchups. That’s been the staple this season, with upsets affecting the rankings each and every week. MORE : Predicting College Football Playoff Rankings Entering Week 12 of 2026 Season Are there any games worth watching? Nov 14, 2026; Columbus, Ohio, USA; Ohio State Buckeyes quarterback Luke Fahey (13) drops to throw during the first quarter against the Northwestern Wildcats at Ohio Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) If you’re a college football lover, you’re going to watch the games either way. But if you’re looking for certain games to watch because of implications, we have you covered. It would be odd to see Ohio State miss the playoff, but that’s looking more likely. However, if the Buckeyes have any shot of making it, they need to take care of business this week against Nebraska and next week against Michigan. Style points are going to matter, and this weekend Ohio State is in Lincoln to play the Huskers. That game will start at Noon ET on Fox, and it’s worth seeing if Ohio State can take a step forward with freshman Luke Fahey behind center. There are implications in the Big 12 and Texas Tech is at the heart of it. The Red Raiders control their own destiny to play Utah, and Texas Tech hits the road against a stingy Baylor defense. That’s at 3:30 p.m. ET on Fox. And while Notre Dame isn’t in a conference, this game was circled several weeks ago. Notre Dame hosts SMU and it’s the Irish’s last game; it feels like they could lose on the schedule. After SMU was blasted last weekend against Wake Forest, it doesn’t feel like a big game, but the Mustangs can put up a lot of points. That game will kick off at 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

Lewis credited the team’s depth after the semifinal. “We’ve got deep, deep personnel,” he said. The challenge is that West’s defense allows 5.5 points per game. Orem can’t afford mistakes, and it needs Curtis to keep the offense on schedule so Lewis isn’t throwing into a secondary that has returned interceptions for touchdowns. Lester Falatea has six interceptions, three defensive touchdowns and seven return touchdowns, which makes him the player most likely to turn the game with one play. Lopati is healthy and running an offense that averages 51.4 points per game. He has completed 70% of his passes for 3,182 yards and 31 touchdowns, and he has run for 832 yards and 12 more, for 43 total touchdowns. Mani Tu’uao averages 23.7 yards per catch and Monson Vaenuku averages 27.8. Naeata Hamilton has run for 1,105 yards and 16 total touchdowns. The biggest concern is discipline. item.description: Rooney scored 53 goals in 120 appearances for England [Getty Images] Warning: This article contains references to suicide Wayne Rooney says he was "contemplating suicide" during his playing days at Manchester United and was "speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up". The former England captain joined United from Everton in 2004 and went on to become the club's record goalscorer, with 253 goals in 559 appearances. But Rooney, speaking with Gabby Logan on the Life at the Midpoint podcast , detailed his struggles off the pitch when eldest son Kai, who is now 17, was a baby. "When I was drinking, I would lock myself in my house for two days and just drink," said Rooney, when asked about the lowest point in his life. "This is probably in my best part of my career playing wise." The 41-year-old went on to explain how he "struggled to deal with it all" and, after opening up to his wife Coleen and his mother, knew he "needed help to get through it". "I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with," he added. "I didn't want Kai seeing me like that, so that's why I'd hide away as well. "I got to a place where you're contemplating suicide. I just didn't want to be around anyone. I didn't want to see people in the streets. I didn't want to go into shops. "I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else, [I] really struggled with it." Rooney, who scored 53 goals in 120 England appearances, was recently named pundit of the year at the Broadcast Sport Awards and is currently appearing on reality TV show I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here. He helped United win five Premier League titles, the Champions League, Europa League, FA Cup and three EFL Cups before leaving them to return to the Toffees in 2017. But the former forward said he learned to mask his feelings during his lowest moments. "You don't want to show any weakness, so you try to mask it," Rooney added. "Even though I knew the position I was in, it was difficult to actually admit that I was in that position because I felt like you feel less of a man, if you like, for doing that. "I was speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up with me because when I look back I was probably at the height of my career, I've just had a young son, I've just been married. "It should be the happiest point in my life and it wasn't. "It was probably the lowest point because of the selfish acts I was taking. "Coleen helped me massively. She could have walked away, it was that bad, but she stuck by me and helped me get through it." item.description: BLOOMINGTON, INDIANA - OCTOBER 17: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes walks off the field after defeating the iu at Memorial Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Bloomington, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the Los Angeles Chargers’ 23-20 win over the Baltimore Ravens last night, the Tennessee Titans now sit atop the 2027 NFL Draft order. Both the Chargers and Titans are 1-8, but the Titans have the easier schedule, so they own the tiebreaker. The Miami Dolphins are the only other 1-win team. They sit at #3 based on strength of schedule. There is still a long way to go before this is final, obviously. It is tough to see the Dolphins winning another game. The Titans aren’t going to win many games, but they will have a good chance to beat the Colts at home in December. I still see the Chargers getting to 3 or 4 wins, so they probably will be a little further down. Right behind those teams, the New York Jets and Philadelphia Eagles sit at two wins. The Jets still have games with the Chargers and Dolphins. They will likely win at least one of those. As for the Eagles, it is impossible to know what the rest of their season is going to look like with their quarterback situation being the way that it is. item.title: Former Yankees ace has strong opinion about Brian Cashman, Aaron Boone | Klapisch
item.description: If anyone has earned the right to weigh in on clubhouse culture, leadership and a manager’s role in maintaining discipline, it’s David Cone . He’s currently the YES Network’s star analyst, but his knowledge was acquired through years in the trenches. No one knows New York baseball like Cone. Do the Yankees need tougher leadership? And what about the scathing indictments from several former Yankees who say the 2026 team lacked an edge? Cone began a lengthy interview on Monday by taking exception to those former Yankees, some of whom were his teammates, for taking uninformed shots at the present-day clubhouse. The list of critics included CC Sabathia, Jorge Posada , Anthony Rizzo and Alex Rodriguez. “I find it really hard to criticize when you’re not in the middle of it, when you’re not in that clubhouse,” Cone said. “It’s easy to take shots when you’re on the outside looking in. We don’t know for sure what goes on behind those closed doors. “It’s a bit surprising hearing all that because ex-players should know better than anyone else. Unless you’re inside the clubhouse, then you really don’t know what’s going on. The ex-players need to be more specific. You need to come with receipts. First, Cone argues Boone couldn’t pull off the tough-guy act even if he tried. “I don’t know if Boone could flip a switch and become that guy overnight and retain any credibility,” Cone said. “That’s not who he is.” Counterargument No. 2 says the bad-cop personality, the kind fans hunger for on social media, no longer exists in baseball. Brewers manager Pat Murphy pulled it off in Milwaukee — and took his team to a world championship. But there’s no one else like him. “I understand the argument, but it’s a bygone era,” Cone said. “How many times do we see managers snap in press conferences anymore? Fights between managers and players? Those days are totally over. You can yearn for that all you want. You want to bring in a hard ass to play a role? Ok, maybe. But the players are going to see right through that. “There’s going to be a credibility issue with that. It has to be natural. It was frustrating, but not disastrous — provided fans account for the obstacles the Yankees faced all summer. “I think not having Judge was the difference,” Cone said. “I mean, the Yankees didn’t have their best players and they still made a decent run. It’s really hard to find position players (at the trade deadline) and Cashman did the best he could. He went outside the box with (Luis) Garcia Jr. He actually gave them a chance. “You have to remember Judge and (Giancarlo) Stanton were supposed to be the firewall against left-handed pitching. An ESPN report published early Monday about how the 41-year-old is handling that slow start turned the focus to his conditioning. item.title: Max Dowman shines in England colours and sends another record tumbling
item.description: Midfielder’s under-21s winner eclipsed Jude Bellingham’s mark and there was other talent to admire against France There may have been an Mbappé on the pitch – Ethan, the younger brother of Kylian, with whom he shares a near-identical gait – but by the end there was only one precocious talent on the lips of those watching England overcome France in their under-21s clash. Max Dowman had done it again, lighting up another game, this time in filthy conditions at Ashton Gate. It was fitting he had the final say in a 3-2 win. The noise that accompanied his match-winning goal? Well, beyond the palpable excitement in the stands in Bristol, that would be the sound of the teenager sending yet another record tumbling. Which one takes your fancy? Take your pick. At 14, playing for Arsenal’s under-19s, he became the Uefa Youth League’s youngest goalscorer. This time last year, after taking to the field at Slavia Prague aged 15 and 308 days, Dowman became the youngest player to feature in the Champions League. In March, six months on from his professional debut, he became the Premier League’s youngest goalscorer. He is the youngest player to earn a Premier League winner’s medal. item.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling. item.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
item.description: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreak Last week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result. Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so. item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. item.description: Visitors take game to world champions and, though their hold on possession plummets, their rearguard is outstanding In the final, absurdly tense moments before England finally did it and Spain finally fell, when Dan Burn had been sent on to do Dan Burn things, when the board had gone up with a 4 on but the clock wasn’t moving fast enough and the men in red kept coming back, Harry Kane had come to the side of the pitch to stand beside Thomas Tuchel. Palms out, Kane signalled and directed and appealed with his teammates to hold on to what they had: s omehow, anyhow . What they had was special, but their grip on it was not as secure as it had seemed. Not as secure as it should have been too. Tuchel gave Kane a nudge that looked pretty playful considering the pressure, before Marc Bollengier, the fourth official, ordered him back to the bench. But England’s captain was not gone for long and when he returned he was joined by almost all of them, awaiting the big moment. From there, he watched James Trafford make an astonishing double save, a moment of heroism that allowed them to hang on. Then, standing alongside the rest who could no longer just sit there, he saw the last header clear – Dan Burn things – before the whistle went. Then he and they went on one last run, back on to the pitch. Continue reading...

item.title: AFC Wimbledon, a failed £87m investment bid and the challenge for fan ownership
item.description: Clubs with wealthy proprietors can maintain a loss-making operation but things can be more complex when the supporters carry the can When you walk up from Haydons Road railway station to Plough Lane there is a blue AFC Wimbledon billboard that reads “Fan owned football”, directly opposite the site of the old Plough Lane stadium where there are now blocks of flats. There is a memorial to the old Wimbledon FC – a reminder that supporters can often have little say in the running of their club – on the same corner, just up the road from the new Cherry Red Records Stadium. AFC Wimbledon are one of only two majority fan-owned clubs in the EFL – along with Exeter – but that makes running a loss‑making operation, as 94% of teams in England’s top five tiers are doing according to the State of the Game report, even more challenging. “In other clubs, the owner just puts their hand in their pocket, produces cash,” said Hannah Kitcher, who has been a member of the Dons Trust Board, which runs AFC Wimbledon, for seven years. “It’s harder when the owners are fans – you can only go to them so many times.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
